instructions: Define the reusable visual system before planning shots: style, identity, locations, props, spatial geometry, light continuity, and reverse-view needs.
Keep project canon in canonical project artifacts; this profile supplies method, never project facts.
Express every planned beat as a visible start state, one primary change, and a visible end state.
Where execution is risky, preserve the story beat through a simpler rescue rather than relying on prose to overcome physical complexity.
Use one coherent camera plan per step and motivate any change in position, framing, or movement from the beat.
Declare blocking, contact, screen direction, spatial anchors, and relevant physical cause-and-effect explicitly.
Store approved identities, state variants, locations, geometry, props, continuity locks, and style truth as named project assets.
Do not turn reusable library recipes into project canon until the project explicitly instantiates and approves them.
Plan the shot against the selected route's resolved capability projection; do not use fixed reference, duration, or cast limits from profile prose.
Record start and end states, primary action, camera plan, blocking, continuity, renderability, risks, and a rescue for every retained material risk.
A start frame represents the exact state at shot time zero and an end frame the exact terminal state, including camera endpoint where relevant.
Approve frames against current project canon and the execution plan, not against a generic library example.
Execute the approved plan and route without inventing alternate actions, camera moves, references, or continuity states.
If the primary approach cannot meet its verification criteria, surface the declared rescue as a production decision.
Review identity, continuity, action, camera, timing, physical contact, and audio separately before judging polish.
Accept or reject against the shot's declared criteria and current canon; a visually attractive mismatch is still a mismatch.

machineRules.message: Generated and AI-enhanced execution requires explicit start and end states.
The execution plan must identify one primary action.
The camera plan must be internally coherent and bound to the planned beat.
Blocking and relevant physical cause-and-effect must be explicit.
Every retained material renderability risk requires a rescue.

provenance.adaptation: Distilled into provider-neutral profile guidance and host predicate identifiers; numerical capability claims were excluded.
